speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: Our project examines instructions hidden in retrieved evidence. We built a two-signal passage gate and evaluated both detection and actual RAG answers. The expanded experiments broaden the source and attack crossing and add an external classifier. The most important new finding is a failure: a gate that retains ordinary emails can still reject legitimate instructions.

speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: Here is an actual attack from our expanded experiment. The user asks how much was paid to Deel. The email reports eight thousand eight hundred and three dollars and fifteen cents, which the clean system answers correctly. An attacker appends a request to ignore the question and print RAG OVERRIDE seven six four. With the same retrieved chunks, the unfiltered system and the probe print that marker. Rules and the combination reject the second chunk and preserve the correct payment amount. The problem matters because a document that should supply facts can redirect the operation the user requested. This example traces that change through an actual generated answer.

speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: We ask three questions. First, can the gate detect injected instructions while preserving legitimate evidence? Second, does combining a learned probe and explicit rule add value over either component and an external detector? Third, does that passage-level benefit transfer to actual answers at a reasonable cost? Our hypothesis is complementary attack coverage. We keep that hypothesis separate from usefulness, because rejecting a chunk can also remove the answer. The evaluation therefore reports attack success, task correctness, benign rejection and computation together. The new legitimate-instruction challenge becomes particularly important when interpreting the headline security result.

speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: Prior work motivates different intervention points. StruQ separates instructions and data using a compatible trained model. Spotlighting signals the provenance of untrusted content. Detection-and-removal methods inspect contaminated text. RobustRAG isolates evidence and aggregates generated answers under a corruption model. Our contribution is narrower: an inspectable gate and a controlled comparison linking its decisions to actual answers, false positives and cost. BIPIA supplies public EmailQA records and attack data. Our retrieval adapter is locally implemented. The external ProtectAI classifier is measured on our test passages rather than represented by its model-card benchmark accuracy.

speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: The attacker edits the email before chunking. A document-scoped TF-IDF retriever returns up to two chunks. BERT stays frozen, a logistic probe scores overlapping windows, and maximum pooling gives passage risk. The explicit cue increases the combined risk; thresholds are selected on development data. Empty retained context returns UNKNOWN, while retained evidence goes to the same Qwen model and greedy decoder. The evaluation has thirty-seven original clean records and one hundred eleven attacked passages. The expanded generator crossing uses thirty-three distinct emails, four templates and both positions. Repeated variants are clustered by email. Exact deterministic response reuse saves computation in the expansion; timing comes from the earlier uncached pilot.

speaker: Weiyi Xia
text: The ROC and precision-recall plots show score ranking across the same held-out passages. At the chosen operating points, the combination detects seventy-four of one hundred eleven attacks, rules sixty-three and the original probe twenty-two. The three local detectors retain the original clean emails. The external DeBERTa wrapper has an AUROC below point five and rejects most clean emails, so we explicitly audited its use rather than treating that result as an ordinary ranking. Mixed-window training improves the probe's AUROC but reduces recall at its validation-selected threshold. Curves, fixed thresholds and benign transfer answer different questions. Our second half connects those detector behaviours to actual answers and the diagnostic failures.

speaker: Xinye He
text: In the expanded crossing, marker successes are 102 without filtering, 16 with rules, 85 with the probe and 7 with the combination, out of two hundred sixty-four variants each. Clean correctness for the combination is 16 of thirty-three. Attacked correctness is 125 of two hundred sixty-four. We report marker exposure and retention separately from output success. The source-email cluster interval describes uncertainty over these thirty-three emails under the fixed templates. The templates are repeated, so the larger variant count is not the same as having two hundred sixty-four independent documents or attack strategies.

speaker: Xinye He
text: The benign-instruction challenge changes the conclusion. It contains twelve ordinary requests or procedures and twelve benign paragraphs using cue-like vocabulary. Rules reject twelve, the original probe twenty-two and the combination all twenty-four. DeBERTa rejects four. The combined gate therefore fails this transfer test despite retaining every ordinary email in the original sample. Instructions such as asking an email recipient to reply, or describing a printer's system message, can be legitimate documentary content. Their wording can still trigger our signals. These authored examples are diagnostic rather than a prevalence estimate, but they are sufficient to reject a broad claim that the gate preserves legitimate instructions.

speaker: Xinye He
text: The external classifier audit confirms SAFE is class zero and INJECTION is class one in both the configuration and actual short controls. We then use the model card's direct input path with a five-hundred-and-twelve-token limit. None of the original passages is truncated. AUROC remains point four one five, with twenty-eight of thirty-seven clean records rejected. The original window wrapper is point four three zero, so removing that wrapper does not solve the anomaly. Four clean financial emails receive high injection scores, while ordinary public task requests score safe in isolation. Their malicious role depends on the payment question. We preserve the raw logits and examples; this points toward transfer and task-context mismatch without proving a unique cause.

speaker: Xinye He
text: The filtering error is concrete. In the earlier uncached pilot's case zero, the correct amount is eight thousand eight hundred and three dollars and fifteen cents. The attacked unfiltered system still gives that amount. Rules and the combination reject the first mixed chunk, keep only the second and answer twenty-five dollars. The suffix example we showed earlier preserves the payment fact instead. Both outcomes involve the same source email but different placement and retained evidence. This is why whole-chunk filtering must be assessed through task correctness as well as marker suppression. The combined gate also costs about one hundred ninety-two milliseconds per request in the uncached CPU measurement.

speaker: Xinye He
text: The expanded experiment covers more documents and every template-position combination, but it still uses one small generator and a fixed four-template attack bank. There is no adaptive attack search or open-corpus poisoning evaluation. The benign challenge changes genre and length relative to the training emails. External classifier calibration also transfers poorly to the original emails. These limits point toward task-conditioned detection, more representative calibration data and evidence-preserving removal. Adding further signals should wait until these basic security and utility failures are addressed.

speaker: Xinye He
text: The signals complement each other on the original attack set, but that coverage does not establish a useful general defence. The expanded system still has seven successful attacks, and the combination rejects all twenty-four legitimate challenge paragraphs. The audited external model also transfers poorly. The public repository preserves source, raw outputs and both positive and negative findings. The next priority is task alignment and evidence preservation.
